name: Dhamma Pajjota
tradition: Vipassana Meditation as taught by S.N. Goenka
technique: Anapana and Vipassana body-scan meditation, taught in silent, structured residential courses
teacherAccess: No individual teacher access; courses are led by certified Goenka-tradition assistant teachers who give recorded evening discourses and are available for brief questions.
retreatOptions: 10-day residential courses for adults (the standard offering, held year-round), plus periodic longer courses for old students, dedicated courses for children and teenagers, and 1-day old-student sittings at nearby satellite locations (Brussels, Bruges, Ghent).
about: Dhamma Pajjota is the first Vipassana center established in the Benelux region, opened in June 2000 in a rural part of Belgian Limburg near Dilsen-Stokkem, close to the borders of the Netherlands and Germany. Its name, given by S.N. Goenka, means "Light" or "Torch" of Dhamma. Set on an 11-acre site with a dedicated meditation hall, the center can accommodate around 110 students and welcomes more than 2,000 people a year to residential courses taught in English alongside Dutch, French, or German. It is run entirely by volunteers through the Belgian non-profit Vipassana vzw and, like all centers in the Goenka network, offers courses completely free of charge, funded solely by the voluntary donations of past students. Students live on-site, observe Noble Silence for most of the course, and follow a fixed daily schedule of meditation and recorded evening discourses.
schedule: 10-day courses run continuously throughout the year, with additional longer courses for old students and separate courses for children and teenagers, all on a fixed published schedule.
cost: No fees of any kind; entirely dana (voluntary donation)-based, with all teaching, food, and lodging given freely and funded by donations from past students.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested amount; a Goenka tradition (dhamma.org) course.

foodNotes: All meals prepared and served on-site at no charge; vegetarian meals included for the full duration of the course.
workNotes: Old students (those who have completed at least one prior 10-day course) are asked to give some work service (dhamma seva) during their stay; new students generally are not required to work.
